title: Compliance failures in acid sale regulation despite strict rules
p1:
Strict rules exist for acid sales. So why do illegal and unsafe sales still happen?

The surprising part is that the biggest gaps often appear not in the law, but in its everyday enforcement.
p2:
Many people assume that a strong regulation automatically prevents misuse. But compliance depends on every step — seller verification, record keeping, reporting, and local monitoring.

A lesser-known fact: even when rules require documentation, weak checks at the ground level can allow violations to continue unnoticed.
p3:
Acid sale regulations are designed to reduce harm by controlling who can purchase these dangerous substances and ensuring accountability from sellers.

The real lesson is that compliance is not just about creating rules. It requires awareness, responsible businesses, regular inspections, and quick action when violations occur.

For businesses, following safety regulations is not only a legal duty but also a responsibility toward society.
